Subject: Logging controls & sensitive-data redaction - follow-up

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciate you walking us through FinTechCo's logging and compliance constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Ask: You said you need assurance that request/response logs will not retain PII (names, account numbers, full SSNs) and that headers and trace IDs can be masked/hashed.
- Current infra constraints: Data must remain in US region for production workloads; retention windows for logs are typically 90 days but security may require 30 days for certain environments.
- Redwood capabilities we discussed: configurable logging levels, field-level redaction on request/response payloads, header masking, and optional trace-id hashing.

Can you send a small sanitized sample of the request/response logs you mentioned (attached is an example format from our side)? Also, confirm whether trace IDs are used for cross-service tracing (we can hash them to preserve correlation without storing raw IDs).

Next steps I propose:
1) You share a sample log (sanitized) and a short list of fields you consider PII.
2) We'll have Rishi and Dev review and produce a short redaction plan (regex/templates + retention policy options).
3) Schedule a 45-min technical workshop (hands-on) to validate the redaction rules against your sample.

Attaching: redwood-logging-controls.pdf (summary of logging options).

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Logging controls & sensitive-data redaction - follow-up

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few points from our side:
- We cannot store unredacted PANs, SSNs, or customer full names in logs. Partial tokenization is acceptable (e.g., last 4 digits for PAN).
- Trace IDs are used across services for debugging; we need correlation for incident investigations but cannot store raw trace IDs. Hashing is OK as long as it is deterministic within a retention window.
- Preferred retention: 30 days for production request/response logs; 365 days for aggregated metrics only.

I've attached a sanitized sample log file (fintechco-sample-logs.txt) showing header examples and request/response pairs. Two quick clarifying Qs:
1) Can Redwood support per-environment retention (e.g., staging 7d, prod 30d)?
2) Do you provide an automated rule test harness so we can validate that redaction rules don't break downstream parsing?

Happy to do the workshop next week; Bob and I are available Tue/Wed mornings PT.

Best,
Alice
Security Engineering Manager | FinTechCo
alice.tan@fintechco.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-12 21:10 PDT
Subject: Internal: FinTechCo logging/redaction next steps

Marissa / Dev —

I reviewed Alice's sample and their asks. High-level notes on what we can commit to and implementation approach: 

- Logging levels: we offer three modes for request/response payloads: none (no payloads), minimal (metadata only), full (payloads stored with redaction templates applied). Mode is configurable per route and per-deployment (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Field redaction: configurable regex-based templates + JSON path masks for structured payloads. We can ship a standard "PII" template (email, phone, PAN, SSN) and allow customer-specific fields.
- Header masking: we can mask Authorization, Cookie, and any header key the customer indicates. Masking replaces values with deterministic hashes or fixed tokens.
- Trace IDs: we can hash trace IDs using a per-customer salt stored in KMS so hashes are deterministic for correlation but not reversible. Hash rotation policy can be tied to retention windows.
- Retention: per-environment retention windows supported, with automatic purge jobs. We can support 7d/30d/365d tiers and allow custom windows via Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Data residency: for production we will ensure logs are stored in the US region; for Dedicated/Private we can support customer VPCs and on-prem options.

Risks/Edge cases: unstructured blobs (base64 attachments) need pattern scanning and may require heavier processing; propose we mark these as "no-store" by default unless requested. Also need to validate that redaction rules don't break SDK consumers relying on specific fields.

Next steps (technical):
- We run their sample against our redaction harness and return a report (false positives/negatives).
- Prepare an agenda for the 45-min workshop: goals, sample run, rule tuning, retention confirmation.

I can own the redaction harness run. Dev, can you prepare the per-route config template and a short demo (10 min) showing header masking + trace-id hashing?

Rishi
Principal Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
